score_1_desc: No dock scheduling exists - inbound trucks arrive whenever the vendor chooses, with no assigned time window and frequent dock congestion.
score_2_desc: A rough scheduling attempt exists (a phone call or message) but isn't tracked, and vendors regularly ignore it.
score_3_desc: A documented dock schedule with assigned time windows per vendor exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Dock scheduling is actively enforced with a booking system or calendar, and vendor adherence is tracked against a KPI.
score_5_desc: Dock scheduling is fully digitized (self-service vendor booking), with real-time visibility and automatic reflow when a slot is missed.

score_1_desc: No record of when inbound trucks actually arrive or when unloading finishes - there's no way to know how long anything sat at the dock.
score_2_desc: Arrival time is noted informally (a scrawled note) but not consistently, and isn't compiled anywhere.
score_3_desc: A documented process for logging arrival and unload-complete times exists and is generally followed, recorded manually or in a spreadsheet.
score_4_desc: Time-stamping is actively reviewed against a dock-to-shelf time KPI, with delays flagged and investigated.
score_5_desc: Time-stamping is automatic (system/scan-based) and dock-to-shelf time is a continuously monitored, benchmarked metric.

score_1_desc: No documented SOP for what happens between a truck arriving and produce reaching storage - the sequence depends entirely on whoever is working.
score_2_desc: An informal sequence is understood by experienced staff but isn't written down, and breaks down when they're absent.
score_3_desc: A documented dock-to-shelf SOP exists and is generally followed under normal conditions.
score_4_desc: SOP adherence is actively audited on a defined cadence, with deviations tracked and corrected.
score_5_desc: The SOP is system-guided (e.g. task prompts) and adherence is consistently near 100%, verified continuously.

score_1_desc: No written grading standard exists for any produce category - acceptance is a purely subjective call.
score_2_desc: A grading standard exists informally in a few people's heads but isn't written down anywhere.
score_3_desc: A documented grading rubric (ripeness, blemish tolerance, size) exists for major SKU categories.
score_4_desc: The grading rubric is actively maintained, covers most SKUs, and is referenced during training.
score_5_desc: Grading standards are documented with photo references for every SKU category and reviewed/updated on a regular cadence.

score_1_desc: Grading is applied inconsistently or not at all - different staff make different calls on the same produce.
score_2_desc: Grading happens but isn't sampling-based or systematic - whoever is at the dock eyeballs a few crates.
score_3_desc: A defined sampling method (e.g. check N crates per batch) is documented and generally followed.
score_4_desc: Sampling-based grading is actively tracked for consistency across shifts/staff, with outliers coached.
score_5_desc: Grading consistency is measured (e.g. inter-rater agreement) and continuously improved through training and feedback.

score_1_desc: Rejected produce is discarded or sent back with no record of quantity, reason, or vendor.
score_2_desc: Rejections are occasionally noted informally but not compiled or shared with vendors.
score_3_desc: A documented process for logging rejections (vendor, SKU, reason, quantity) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Rejection data is actively reviewed and shared with vendors on a defined cadence, feeding into vendor scorecards.
score_5_desc: Rejection data automatically feeds vendor performance reviews and sourcing decisions, with trends tracked over time.

score_1_desc: No batch or lot identification happens at receiving - once inside the facility, produce origin is untraceable.
score_2_desc: Batch/lot tagging happens manually and inconsistently (marker on a box), often illegible or lost.
score_3_desc: A documented batch-tagging process (vendor, date, lot) exists and is applied consistently.
score_4_desc: Batch tagging is actively verified at receiving with a defined accuracy target.
score_5_desc: Batch/lot identification is barcode/QR-based and system-captured at the point of receiving.

score_1_desc: Once a batch is put away, there's no way to trace it - stock is treated as a single undifferentiated pool.
score_2_desc: Some batches can be traced with effort (asking staff, checking notes) but it's unreliable.
score_3_desc: A documented process keeps batch identity associated with stock through storage, generally followed.
score_4_desc: Batch traceability through storage is actively spot-checked and discrepancies are investigated.
score_5_desc: Full batch-level traceability is system-enforced from receiving through storage to pick, queryable instantly.

score_1_desc: If a quality issue is found downstream, there's no way to trace it back to a specific inbound batch or vendor.
score_2_desc: Root-cause tracing is possible in theory but takes significant manual effort and often fails.
score_3_desc: A documented process exists to trace a downstream issue back to its batch/vendor, generally workable within a reasonable time.
score_4_desc: Traceability is actively tested/drilled on a defined cadence to confirm it actually works when needed.
score_5_desc: Any downstream issue can be traced to its exact inbound batch and vendor within minutes, system-supported.

score_1_desc: No temperature sensors installed anywhere in storage - conditions are assumed, never measured.
score_2_desc: A single sensor exists somewhere in the facility, not representative of conditions across different storage zones.
score_3_desc: Sensors are placed in each defined storage zone per a documented placement plan, generally followed.
score_4_desc: Sensor placement is actively reviewed against hot-spot/cold-spot mapping and adjusted when gaps are found.
score_5_desc: Sensor coverage is continuously validated (calibration checks, redundancy in critical zones) and placement is data-driven from historical temperature variance.

score_1_desc: Temperature is never logged - if it's checked at all, it's a glance with no record kept.
score_2_desc: Readings are taken irregularly and logged inconsistently, often skipped during busy periods.
score_3_desc: A documented reading schedule (e.g. every 2 hours) exists and logs are generally kept, manually or in a spreadsheet.
score_4_desc: Reading frequency is actively enforced with completion tracked against the schedule, gaps flagged.
score_5_desc: Readings are continuous and automatic (sensor-logged), with 100% time-coverage and no manual step required.

score_1_desc: No defined response when temperature goes out of range - it's noticed only if someone happens to check.
score_2_desc: An informal response exists ("tell the supervisor") but isn't documented or consistently followed.
score_3_desc: A documented escalation process (who's notified, what action is taken) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Escalations are actively tracked with response-time targets, and root causes of excursions are reviewed.
score_5_desc: Excursions trigger automatic real-time alerts with a defined SLA for response, and escalation effectiveness is continuously measured.

score_1_desc: No storage zones are defined at all - the facility is one undifferentiated space.
score_2_desc: Zones exist informally ("the cold corner") but aren't labeled or documented anywhere.
score_3_desc: Zones are documented and physically labeled, with a written guide for what belongs where.
score_4_desc: Zone definitions are actively reviewed and refined based on operational experience, with staff trained on them.
score_5_desc: Zone layout is data-optimized (temperature mapping, produce mix) and digitally referenced in the WMS.

score_1_desc: No awareness of ethylene sensitivity - gas-producing and gas-sensitive produce are stored together routinely, accelerating spoilage.
score_2_desc: Ethylene sensitivity is known informally by some staff but not applied systematically.
score_3_desc: A documented ethylene-compatibility guide exists and separation is generally practiced.
score_4_desc: Ethylene separation is actively audited and violations are tracked back to spoilage outcomes.
score_5_desc: Ethylene management is systematized (zone assignment enforces it automatically) and continuously validated against spoilage data.

score_1_desc: Produce is put away wherever there's space, regardless of defined zones.
score_2_desc: Staff generally know where things should go but zoning isn't checked or enforced.
score_3_desc: A documented put-away process references zone assignment and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Zone compliance at put-away is actively spot-checked, with misplacement tracked and corrected.
score_5_desc: Zone assignment is system-enforced at put-away (WMS blocks incorrect placement).

score_1_desc: No humidity targets exist for any zone - humidity is whatever it happens to be.
score_2_desc: A rough humidity preference exists informally but isn't documented or measured against.
score_3_desc: Documented humidity targets exist per zone/produce category and are referenced.
score_4_desc: Humidity is actively measured against targets with corrective action when out of range.
score_5_desc: Humidity targets are continuously refined based on spoilage outcomes and automatically enforced per zone.

score_1_desc: No ventilation equipment maintenance - fans/humidifiers run (or don't) with no upkeep plan.
score_2_desc: Equipment is fixed reactively only after visible failure, with no preventive maintenance.
score_3_desc: A documented maintenance schedule exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Maintenance completion is actively tracked against the schedule, with equipment downtime monitored.
score_5_desc: Maintenance is predictive/condition-based, with equipment performance continuously monitored and downtime near zero.

score_1_desc: Slotting ignores sales velocity entirely - fast and slow movers are placed identically, with no regard to picker travel time.
score_2_desc: Fast movers are placed conveniently based on staff habit, not documented or data-driven.
score_3_desc: A documented slotting plan based on velocity tiers exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Slot assignment is actively reviewed against current velocity data on a defined cadence and adjusted.
score_5_desc: Slotting is dynamically optimized by an algorithm/system recommendation based on real-time velocity.

score_1_desc: Placement ignores shelf-life entirely - short-life items can end up in the slowest-to-reach locations.
score_2_desc: Shelf-life is considered informally by experienced staff but not systematically.
score_3_desc: A documented placement rule links shelf-life to proximity (shortest-life nearest pack-out) and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Shelf-life-aware placement is actively audited and adjusted based on spoilage patterns.
score_5_desc: Placement is system-recommended based on live shelf-life data per batch.

score_1_desc: No time-to-shelf target exists - produce can sit unshelved for an unpredictable, untracked duration.
score_2_desc: A rough expectation exists informally but isn't measured.
score_3_desc: A documented time-to-shelf target exists and is occasionally checked.
score_4_desc: Time-to-shelf is actively measured against the target with delays investigated.
score_5_desc: Time-to-shelf is continuously tracked in real time and benchmarked against a best-in-class threshold.

score_1_desc: Staffing doesn't flex with inbound volume at all - peak periods cause the same delays every time with no adjustment.
score_2_desc: Staffing is adjusted informally and inconsistently when someone notices a backlog.
score_3_desc: A documented staffing plan for peak inbound periods exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Staffing response is actively reviewed against actual peak performance and refined.
score_5_desc: Staffing is dynamically planned using inbound forecast data, with peak delays minimized proactively.

score_1_desc: No date labeling on bins or locations - there's no way to tell which stock is older without digging through it.
score_2_desc: Some batches are dated informally (marker on a box) but inconsistently.
score_3_desc: A documented date-labeling process exists and is generally applied.
score_4_desc: Date-labeling accuracy is actively spot-checked and corrected.
score_5_desc: Date labeling is barcode/system-based and automatically visible at the point of pick.

score_1_desc: Pickers grab whichever unit is easiest to reach, with no regard to which batch is older.
score_2_desc: FEFO is understood informally but frequently skipped under time pressure.
score_3_desc: A documented FEFO picking process exists and is generally followed with spot checks.
score_4_desc: FEFO adherence is actively audited on a schedule, with violations tracked and coached.
score_5_desc: FEFO is system-directed at pick (the WMS routes pickers to the oldest eligible batch) with adherence near 100%.

score_1_desc: No shelf-life is recorded per batch - there's no way to know how close any given unit is to expiry.
score_2_desc: Shelf-life is estimated by appearance rather than recorded from receipt date.
score_3_desc: A documented shelf-life standard per SKU (days from receipt) is defined and used to track batches.
score_4_desc: Remaining shelf-life is actively tracked per batch and reviewed on a defined cadence.
score_5_desc: Shelf-life is tracked per batch in a system that computes remaining life automatically from receipt date.

score_1_desc: Aging stock is only noticed once it's visibly spoiling - no proactive flagging happens at all.
score_2_desc: Aging stock is occasionally noticed informally but no consistent action is taken.
score_3_desc: A documented process flags aging stock at a defined threshold and prescribes an action (markdown, priority pick).
score_4_desc: Aging-stock flags are actively actioned and tracked to completion, with outcomes reviewed.
score_5_desc: Aging stock is automatically flagged and routed (markdown, redistribution, priority pick) with no manual step.

score_1_desc: No cycle counting happens - stock records and physical stock are never reconciled until a pick fails.
score_2_desc: Counts happen occasionally and informally with no defined schedule or coverage.
score_3_desc: A documented cycle-count schedule (e.g. weekly per zone) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Count completion is actively tracked against the schedule with coverage gaps flagged.
score_5_desc: Cycle counting is continuous/perpetual, system-driven, with full SKU coverage on a rolling basis.

score_1_desc: Count variances are recorded (if at all) with no investigation into why they happened.
score_2_desc: Variances are occasionally looked into informally, without a consistent process.
score_3_desc: A documented variance-investigation process exists and is generally followed for significant variances.
score_4_desc: Variance root causes are actively tracked and trends reviewed to prevent recurrence.
score_5_desc: Variance investigation is systematic and data-driven, with root-cause patterns feeding process improvements automatically.

score_1_desc: Replenishment is purely reactive - triggered only after a stockout is noticed.
score_2_desc: A rough par level exists informally but isn't consistently used to trigger replenishment.
score_3_desc: A documented par level/trigger threshold exists per SKU category and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Trigger thresholds are actively reviewed against sell-through data and adjusted.
score_5_desc: Replenishment triggers are dynamically calculated from real-time sell-through and shelf-life data.

score_1_desc: Replenishment doesn't adjust for known demand spikes at all - promotions and peak periods cause the same stockouts every time.
score_2_desc: Adjustments happen informally and inconsistently when someone remembers an upcoming promotion.
score_3_desc: A documented process adjusts replenishment ahead of known demand drivers and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Peak/promo adjustments are actively reviewed post-event for accuracy and refined.
score_5_desc: Demand-driver adjustments are modeled and applied automatically based on historical promo/peak performance.

score_1_desc: No real sales data feeds the order quantity - it's guessed or copied from the last order.
score_2_desc: Recent sales are referenced informally but not systematically incorporated.
score_3_desc: A documented forecasting input (recent sales trend) is used consistently.
score_4_desc: Forecast inputs are actively validated for quality and expanded to include more signals (weather, day-of-week).
score_5_desc: Forecast inputs are comprehensive and automatically ingested (sales, seasonality, promotions, external signals).

score_1_desc: Forecast accuracy is never checked - there's no feedback loop between predicted and actual demand.
score_2_desc: Accuracy is occasionally noticed informally when a big miss happens.
score_3_desc: A documented review cadence compares forecast to actuals and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Forecast accuracy is actively tracked as a KPI, with systematic adjustments based on error patterns.
score_5_desc: Forecast accuracy is continuously monitored with automated model refinement based on error trends.

score_1_desc: Stockouts aren't tracked at all - it's unclear which SKUs or times are most affected.
score_2_desc: Stockouts are noticed anecdotally but not measured.
score_3_desc: A documented stockout rate is tracked at a basic level per SKU category.
score_4_desc: Stockout rate is actively monitored against a target, with root causes reviewed.
score_5_desc: Stockout rate is tracked in real time per SKU/store with automated root-cause tagging.

score_1_desc: Overstock and the spoilage it causes are never connected - they're treated as unrelated problems.
score_2_desc: The link is occasionally noticed informally but not tracked.
score_3_desc: A documented process tracks spoilage attributable to overstock at a basic level.
score_4_desc: Overstock-linked spoilage is actively monitored and used to adjust replenishment parameters.
score_5_desc: Overstock and spoilage are jointly optimized in a single system view, continuously tuned to minimize both.

score_1_desc: No weighing equipment exists for loose/weighted produce - quantities are estimated by eye.
score_2_desc: Some weighing equipment exists but isn't consistently used or calibrated.
score_3_desc: A documented weighing process with calibrated scales exists at defined stations and is generally used.
score_4_desc: Scale calibration and usage are actively audited on a schedule.
score_5_desc: Weighing is integrated into the pick workflow (system-connected scales) with calibration continuously monitored.

score_1_desc: No tolerance standard exists for weighted picks - over/under-fulfillment is common and unmeasured.
score_2_desc: A rough tolerance is understood informally but not enforced or measured.
score_3_desc: A documented tolerance band exists per SKU and is generally referenced.
score_4_desc: Tolerance adherence is actively measured against a KPI, with deviations tracked to individual pickers.
score_5_desc: Tolerance is system-verified at pack (automatic flag on out-of-tolerance) with accuracy consistently best-in-class.

score_1_desc: No packaging standard exists - packaging choice is left entirely to whoever is packing.
score_2_desc: A rough packaging preference exists for a few fragile items but isn't documented.
score_3_desc: A documented packaging standard per produce category exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Packaging standards are actively reviewed against damage data and refined.
score_5_desc: Packaging is continuously optimized per SKU based on transit-damage analytics.

score_1_desc: Transit damage isn't tracked - complaints or returns are handled case by case with no pattern analysis.
score_2_desc: Damage is occasionally noted informally but not compiled.
score_3_desc: A documented process logs transit damage (SKU, cause) and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Damage data is actively reviewed and fed back into packaging decisions on a defined cadence.
score_5_desc: Damage tracking is real-time and automatically triggers packaging standard updates.

score_1_desc: Spoiled produce is discarded with no record of quantity, SKU, or cause at all.
score_2_desc: Spoilage is estimated informally rather than logged consistently.
score_3_desc: A documented logging process (SKU, quantity, reason) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Spoilage logging completeness is actively audited and gaps are corrected.
score_5_desc: Spoilage is logged in real time per SKU/batch with automated reporting.

score_1_desc: There's no shrinkage percentage calculated at all - spoilage cost is invisible.
score_2_desc: Shrinkage is estimated roughly but not calculated as a consistent percentage of throughput.
score_3_desc: Shrinkage % is calculated on a defined cadence and compared to a basic target.
score_4_desc: Shrinkage % is actively tracked as a KPI and reviewed against a best-in-class benchmark.
score_5_desc: Shrinkage % is tracked in real time and directly feeds sourcing/replenishment decisions.

score_1_desc: Spoilage causes are never categorized - it's treated as an unavoidable cost, not a solvable problem.
score_2_desc: Causes are occasionally guessed at informally.
score_3_desc: A documented categorization (over-order, cold-chain break, aged stock, damage) exists and is generally applied.
score_4_desc: Cause categorization is actively analyzed for patterns and reviewed on a defined cadence.
score_5_desc: Cause categorization is systematic and data-driven, with patterns surfaced automatically.

score_1_desc: No corrective actions are taken based on spoilage causes - the same problems recur unaddressed.
score_2_desc: Corrective actions are occasionally taken informally but not tracked to completion.
score_3_desc: A documented process assigns and tracks corrective actions for identified causes.
score_4_desc: Corrective action effectiveness is actively measured and reviewed.
score_5_desc: Corrective actions are automatically prioritized by impact and their effectiveness is tracked continuously.

score_1_desc: Stock disappears from the floor with no formal write-off, approval, or verification at all.
score_2_desc: Write-offs are recorded informally and inconsistently, often without approval.
score_3_desc: A documented write-off SOP (verification, approval) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Write-off approvals are actively audited for compliance with the SOP.
score_5_desc: Write-off approval is system-integrated and fully auditable, with no manual gaps.

score_1_desc: Disposed stock is never reconciled against inventory records - the system and reality drift apart silently.
score_2_desc: Reconciliation happens occasionally and informally.
score_3_desc: A documented reconciliation process runs on a defined cadence and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Reconciliation is actively monitored for unusual patterns, which are investigated.
score_5_desc: Reconciliation is automatic and real-time, with disposal method also optimized (e.g. donation/composting) to reduce cost and waste impact.

score_1_desc: No receiving discipline at the collection center - produce is dropped off with no check-in, weighing, or condition assessment.
score_2_desc: A rough check-in happens informally at some centers but isn't consistent or recorded.
score_3_desc: A documented CC receiving process (check-in, weigh, basic condition check) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: CC receiving is actively audited against the SOP, with compliance tracked per center.
score_5_desc: CC receiving is standardized and digitally logged across all centers, with real-time visibility into intake quality.

score_1_desc: No handling standard for the CC-to-warehouse leg - produce travels however it happens to be loaded, with frequent transit damage/quality loss.
score_2_desc: A rough transit practice exists informally (e.g. "use the covered truck when available") but isn't documented.
score_3_desc: A documented transit handling standard (vehicle type, loading practice, timing) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Transit handling is actively monitored (condition-on-arrival vs condition-at-CC) with deviations investigated.
score_5_desc: Transit is continuously monitored (temperature-logged vehicles where relevant) with condition loss tracked and minimized as a KPI.

score_1_desc: No vendor scorecard exists - sourcing decisions don't reference any tracked performance history.
score_2_desc: A scorecard concept exists informally but isn't consistently populated or referenced.
score_3_desc: A documented vendor scorecard (quality, rejection rate, on-time %) exists and is generally used.
score_4_desc: The scorecard is actively reviewed on a defined cadence and directly informs sourcing allocation decisions.
score_5_desc: The scorecard is continuously updated and automatically weights sourcing decisions, with vendors given visibility into their own standing.

score_1_desc: New vendors are onboarded with no capability assessment at all - quality and reliability are discovered after the fact.
score_2_desc: A rough informal check happens before onboarding some vendors, but isn't consistent or documented.
score_3_desc: A documented onboarding/capability assessment process exists and is generally applied to new vendors.
score_4_desc: Onboarding assessments are actively tracked against subsequent actual performance to validate the process.
score_5_desc: Onboarding is standardized, data-driven, and continuously refined based on which onboarding signals actually predict performance.

score_1_desc: No flow pattern is defined - inbound, storage, and outbound activity happen wherever there's space, with paths crossing constantly.
score_2_desc: A flow pattern is understood informally by long-tenured staff but was never deliberately designed or documented.
score_3_desc: A documented flow pattern (e.g. U-shaped or criss-cross) is defined for the facility and generally followed.
score_4_desc: The flow pattern is actively validated against actual movement (walk-throughs, timing studies) and refined.
score_5_desc: Flow pattern is data-optimized and periodically re-validated as volume/SKU mix changes.

score_1_desc: Cross-traffic between inbound, picking, and dispatch activity is unmanaged - collisions and bottlenecks are a routine part of the day.
score_2_desc: Congestion is addressed reactively and informally in the moment, with no underlying process change.
score_3_desc: A documented approach to managing cross-traffic (staggered timing, designated paths) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Congestion points are actively tracked and addressed through layout or scheduling changes.
score_5_desc: Cross-traffic is continuously monitored and proactively managed through dynamic scheduling/routing.

score_1_desc: Docks are used on a first-come basis with no allocation logic at all, causing frequent conflicts.
score_2_desc: A rough informal priority exists (e.g. "regular vendors get first dock") but isn't documented.
score_3_desc: A documented dock allocation logic (by vendor, time window, or activity type) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Dock allocation effectiveness is actively measured (wait time, conflicts) and the logic is refined.
score_5_desc: Dock allocation is system-scheduled and dynamically adjusted based on real-time conditions.

score_1_desc: Slot/dock utilization is never measured - there's no visibility into how much idle or conflict time exists.
score_2_desc: Utilization is estimated informally ("docks always seem busy") without real measurement.
score_3_desc: A documented process tracks slot utilization on a basic level (e.g. logged manually).
score_4_desc: Utilization is actively tracked as a KPI and reviewed to identify chronic bottleneck slots/times.
score_5_desc: Utilization is tracked continuously and automatically surfaces bottlenecks for proactive resolution.

score_1_desc: Rejected goods aren't physically segregated at all - they can end up mixed back into accepted stock by mistake.
score_2_desc: Segregation happens informally (a corner is used) but isn't a defined, labeled holding area.
score_3_desc: A documented segregation process (labeled holding area, clear marking) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Segregation compliance is actively audited, with any mixing incidents investigated.
score_5_desc: Segregation is system-enforced (rejected stock can't be picked or shipped) and continuously verified.

score_1_desc: No decision process exists for what happens to rejected goods - the outcome varies by whoever is handling it that day.
score_2_desc: A rough informal rule exists ("just send it back") but isn't documented or applied consistently.
score_3_desc: A documented disposition decision process (return to vendor / downgrade / dispose) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Disposition decisions are actively tracked and reviewed for cost-effectiveness.
score_5_desc: Disposition decisions are rule-based and system-guided, optimized for cost and waste reduction.

score_1_desc: Vendors are never told why a shipment was rejected - they have no way to correct the underlying issue.
score_2_desc: Communication happens informally and inconsistently, often verbal and undocumented.
score_3_desc: A documented process communicates specific rejection reasons to the vendor and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Communication is actively tracked for completeness and timeliness.
score_5_desc: Rejection reasons are automatically communicated to vendors in real time, with a documented trail.

score_1_desc: Rejection data isn't analyzed for trends at all - repeated issues from the same vendor/SKU go unnoticed.
score_2_desc: Trends are occasionally noticed informally but not systematically analyzed.
score_3_desc: A documented process reviews rejection trends by vendor/SKU on a defined cadence.
score_4_desc: Rejection trends actively inform vendor scorecard updates and sourcing decisions.
score_5_desc: Rejection trend analysis is continuous and automatically flags vendors/SKUs crossing a risk threshold.

score_1_desc: No SOP exists for receiving returns - they're accepted back with no condition check or documentation.
score_2_desc: A rough informal check happens but isn't documented or consistently applied.
score_3_desc: A documented return-receiving SOP (condition check, reason capture) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Return receiving compliance is actively audited against the SOP.
score_5_desc: Return receiving is standardized and digitally logged, with condition data captured systematically.

score_1_desc: Returned goods have no defined next step - restock, dispose, and write-off decisions are made inconsistently.
score_2_desc: Disposition happens informally based on whoever is handling the return.
score_3_desc: A documented disposition process (restock if sellable / dispose / write-off) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Disposition decisions are actively tracked and reviewed for accuracy and cost impact.
score_5_desc: Disposition is rule-based and system-guided, with outcomes tracked against sellability criteria.

score_1_desc: No record is kept of why anything is returned - the data simply doesn't exist.
score_2_desc: Reasons are occasionally noted informally but not compiled anywhere.
score_3_desc: A documented process logs return reasons in a structured way and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Return reasons are actively categorized and reviewed on a defined cadence.
score_5_desc: Return reason tracking is systematic and real-time, feeding directly into upstream process dashboards.

score_1_desc: Nothing upstream ever changes in response to returns - the same causes keep producing the same returns.
score_2_desc: Corrections happen occasionally and informally when a pattern becomes impossible to ignore.
score_3_desc: A documented process links return root causes to corrective action in the relevant upstream area.
score_4_desc: Corrective actions from returns are actively tracked to completion and their impact measured.
score_5_desc: Return-driven correction is systematic, with root causes automatically routed and impact continuously tracked.

score_1_desc: Complaints are not logged at all - if a customer complains, it's handled and then lost with no record.
score_2_desc: Complaints are logged informally and inconsistently, often missing key details.
score_3_desc: A documented complaint-logging process exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Complaint logging completeness is actively audited and gaps are corrected.
score_5_desc: Complaint logging is systematic and structured, capturing full detail automatically at the point of complaint.

score_1_desc: There's no way to trace a complaint back to a specific batch, vendor, or process step.
score_2_desc: Tracing back is possible in theory with significant manual effort, and often fails.
score_3_desc: A documented process links complaints to batch/vendor data where available, generally workable.
score_4_desc: Traceability is actively tested to confirm it works, with gaps addressed.
score_5_desc: Any complaint can be traced to its source batch/vendor within minutes, system-supported.

score_1_desc: No one owns complaint resolution - complaints can sit indefinitely with no accountable person.
score_2_desc: Ownership is informal and inconsistent, varying by who happens to pick it up.
score_3_desc: A documented process assigns ownership and a time target for resolution, generally followed.
score_4_desc: Resolution time is actively tracked against the target, with overdue items flagged and escalated.
score_5_desc: Resolution ownership and time are system-tracked with automatic escalation on breach.

score_1_desc: Complaints and wastage/spoilage data are tracked completely separately, if at all - no one looks at whether they're related.
score_2_desc: A connection is occasionally noticed informally but never analyzed.
score_3_desc: A documented process reviews complaints alongside wastage data on a basic level.
score_4_desc: Complaint-wastage correlation is actively analyzed to find shared root causes.
score_5_desc: Complaints and wastage are tracked in one unified dashboard (hub-wise), with correlation continuously monitored.

score_1_desc: No operational policies are documented anywhere - practices exist only as tribal knowledge.
score_2_desc: Some policies are written down but aren't distributed or referenced consistently.
score_3_desc: Documented policies exist and are distributed to relevant staff, generally referenced.
score_4_desc: Policy adherence is actively audited, with gaps between policy and practice corrected.
score_5_desc: Policies are centrally maintained, versioned, and automatically distributed/updated across all sites.

score_1_desc: No regular monitoring rhythm exists - operations are reviewed only when something goes visibly wrong.
score_2_desc: Monitoring happens informally and inconsistently, without a defined schedule.
score_3_desc: A documented daily/weekly monitoring rhythm exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Monitoring rhythm adherence is actively tracked, with findings reviewed and actioned.
score_5_desc: Monitoring is continuous and dashboard-driven, with the rhythm automated rather than manually run.

score_1_desc: No thresholds are defined for any operational metric - there's no line between "normal" and "needs attention."
score_2_desc: Rough thresholds exist informally in experienced staff's judgment, not documented.
score_3_desc: Documented thresholds exist for key metrics and are generally referenced.
score_4_desc: Thresholds are actively reviewed and recalibrated based on operational experience.
score_5_desc: Thresholds are data-derived, continuously recalibrated, and applied automatically across all monitored metrics.

score_1_desc: When something is escalated, there's no defined response process or expectation of closure.
score_2_desc: Escalations are handled informally and inconsistently, often without being tracked to closure.
score_3_desc: A documented escalation-response process exists (who responds, in what time) and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Escalation response time and closure are actively tracked against targets.
score_5_desc: Escalations are system-tracked end to end with automatic reminders and closure verification.

score_1_desc: No one is tracking daily market conditions (prices, availability, quality) at all.
score_2_desc: Some market awareness exists informally through individual relationships, not systematically captured.
score_3_desc: A documented process for daily market intelligence capture exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Market intelligence capture is actively reviewed for completeness and accuracy.
score_5_desc: Market intelligence is captured systematically from multiple sources and available in near real time.

score_1_desc: Sourcing and planning don't account for seasonality at all - the same approach is used year-round regardless of season.
score_2_desc: Seasonal adjustments happen informally based on individual experience.
score_3_desc: A documented seasonal adjustment process (product, sourcing area, special instructions) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Seasonal adjustments are actively reviewed for effectiveness after each season and refined.
score_5_desc: Seasonal adjustment is data-driven, using historical performance to proactively plan ahead of each season.

score_1_desc: No benchmark companies are tracked at all - there's no external reference for quality, margins, or variability standards.
score_2_desc: Some informal awareness of competitors/benchmarks exists but isn't documented or tracked.
score_3_desc: A documented list of benchmark companies (by customer type, quality, margins, variability) exists and is referenced.
score_4_desc: Benchmark tracking is actively updated and used to inform strategic decisions.
score_5_desc: Benchmark tracking is continuous and systematically maintained, directly informing target-setting.

score_1_desc: No hub-wise SKU list or sorting & grading norms exist - every hub operates by its own undocumented standard.
score_2_desc: A rough SKU/norm understanding exists informally per hub, not documented or consistent across hubs.
score_3_desc: A documented hub-wise SKU list and S&G norms exist and are generally followed.
score_4_desc: Hub-wise norms are actively reviewed and reconciled across hubs for consistency.
score_5_desc: Hub-wise SKU lists and norms are centrally maintained and kept continuously consistent across all hubs.

score_1_desc: No role-specific training curriculum exists - training content (if any) is generic or non-existent.
score_2_desc: Some role-specific guidance exists informally but isn't documented as a curriculum.
score_3_desc: A documented role-based training curriculum exists and is generally used for new hires.
score_4_desc: The curriculum is actively reviewed against actual role requirements and updated.
score_5_desc: Curriculum is continuously refined based on performance outcomes and kept current with role changes.

score_1_desc: Training content has no connection to documented SOPs - what's taught and what's supposed to happen can diverge completely.
score_2_desc: Some overlap exists informally between training and SOPs, but they aren't deliberately linked.
score_3_desc: A documented process links training content directly to current SOPs and is generally maintained.
score_4_desc: The SOP-training linkage is actively audited whenever SOPs change.
score_5_desc: Training content is automatically flagged for update whenever the linked SOP changes.

score_1_desc: No record exists of who has completed what training - there's no way to know who's actually trained.
score_2_desc: Completion is tracked informally and inconsistently, often just a memory of who attended.
score_3_desc: A documented completion-tracking process exists and is generally maintained.
score_4_desc: Completion is actively tracked against a target (e.g. 100% of new hires within X days) and gaps are chased.
score_5_desc: Completion tracking is systematic and automated, with real-time visibility into training status per employee.

score_1_desc: No check happens after training to confirm the person actually learned the material - completion is assumed to equal competency.
score_2_desc: A rough informal check happens sometimes (a supervisor watching briefly) but isn't consistent.
score_3_desc: A documented competency check (test, supervised trial) exists after training and is generally applied.
score_4_desc: Competency check results are actively tracked and used to identify training gaps.
score_5_desc: Competency verification is systematic and required before independent work, with results feeding curriculum improvement.

score_1_desc: No relationship exists between headcount and actual volume - staffing levels are set arbitrarily.
score_2_desc: Headcount is adjusted informally based on gut feel when things feel busy or slow.
score_3_desc: A documented headcount plan tied to volume bands exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Headcount vs volume is actively tracked and reviewed for efficiency, with adjustments made proactively.
score_5_desc: Headcount planning is data-driven and continuously calibrated against forecasted and actual volume.

score_1_desc: No flexibility exists for peak periods - the same staffing runs regardless of known demand spikes.
score_2_desc: Extra staffing is arranged informally and inconsistently when a peak is remembered in advance.
score_3_desc: A documented plan for peak-period staffing (temp staff, shift extensions) exists and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Peak staffing effectiveness is actively reviewed post-event and refined.
score_5_desc: Peak staffing is proactively planned from demand forecasts, with flexibility built into standing contracts/processes.

score_1_desc: No role definitions exist - who's responsible for what is unclear and constantly renegotiated day to day.
score_2_desc: Roles are understood informally by tenured staff but not documented anywhere.
score_3_desc: Documented role/responsibility definitions exist and are generally referenced.
score_4_desc: Role clarity is actively checked (e.g. via staff surveys or audits) and gaps are corrected.
score_5_desc: Roles are clearly documented, continuously reinforced through training, and reviewed as operations evolve.

score_1_desc: Attrition isn't tracked at all - staff turnover happens with no visibility into rate or cause.
score_2_desc: Attrition is noticed informally ("we're always hiring") without being measured.
score_3_desc: A documented process tracks attrition rate and basic exit reasons.
score_4_desc: Attrition is actively analyzed for root causes and response actions are taken.
score_5_desc: Attrition is tracked continuously with root-cause analysis directly informing retention initiatives.

score_1_desc: No metrics are defined for most operational areas - there's nothing to even measure against.
score_2_desc: A few metrics exist informally for the areas someone happened to care about.
score_3_desc: A documented set of metrics covers the key operational areas and is generally maintained.
score_4_desc: Metric coverage is actively reviewed for gaps and expanded where needed.
score_5_desc: Metric definitions are comprehensive, consistently maintained, and reviewed for relevance on a regular cadence.

score_1_desc: No metric has a defined owner - if something isn't tracked or acted on, there's no one accountable.
score_2_desc: Ownership is assumed informally rather than assigned.
score_3_desc: A documented ownership assignment exists for key metrics and is generally respected.
score_4_desc: Ownership is actively reinforced, with owners accountable for reviewing and acting on their metrics.
score_5_desc: Every metric has a clear, current owner who is accountable and actively reviewed on metric performance.

score_1_desc: No dashboard exists for any operational metric - performance data, if it exists, lives in scattered files no one checks.
score_2_desc: A basic dashboard/report exists but is updated inconsistently and often stale.
score_3_desc: A documented dashboard with a defined refresh cadence exists and is generally maintained.
score_4_desc: Dashboard freshness and accuracy are actively monitored, with issues corrected quickly.
score_5_desc: Dashboards are real-time or near-real-time, comprehensive, and reliably available to all who need them.

score_1_desc: Metrics, even when tracked, don't actually inform any decisions - operations run the same regardless of what the numbers say.
score_2_desc: Metrics occasionally inform a decision informally, but it's not a consistent practice.
score_3_desc: A documented process references metrics in regular operational decision-making and is generally followed.
score_4_desc: Metric-driven decisions are actively tracked, with outcomes reviewed to confirm the metric was the right one to act on.
score_5_desc: Decision-making is systematically metric-driven, with a demonstrated track record of metrics changing operational behavior.

score_1_desc: No cost-per-unit figure is tracked for any part of the operation - unit economics are unknown at the operational level.
score_2_desc: A rough cost estimate exists informally but isn't calculated consistently.
score_3_desc: A documented cost-per-unit tracking process exists for key activities and is generally maintained.
score_4_desc: Cost-per-unit is actively tracked against a target and reviewed regularly.
score_5_desc: Cost-per-unit is tracked in real time across activities and directly informs operational decisions.

score_1_desc: There's no target or benchmark to compare actual costs against - cost performance can't be judged as good or bad.
score_2_desc: A rough informal sense of "reasonable cost" exists without a defined benchmark.
score_3_desc: Documented cost benchmarks/targets exist and actual costs are generally compared against them.
score_4_desc: Cost-vs-benchmark variance is actively reviewed and drives corrective action.
score_5_desc: Cost benchmarking is continuous and automatically flags variance for action.

score_1_desc: The cost of spoilage and rejections is never quantified in currency terms - only the physical quantity (if that) is known.
score_2_desc: A rough cost estimate is made informally and inconsistently.
score_3_desc: A documented process converts spoilage/rejection quantities into a cost figure on a basic level.
score_4_desc: Cost quantification is actively tracked and reviewed against a reduction target.
score_5_desc: Spoilage/rejection cost is quantified in real time and automatically prioritized against other cost drivers.

score_1_desc: Cost impact of quality failures is never reported to anyone beyond the immediate team, if it's tracked at all.
score_2_desc: Reporting happens informally and inconsistently, often only when something goes badly wrong.
score_3_desc: A documented reporting process shares cost-of-quality-failure with stakeholders on a defined cadence.
score_4_desc: Reporting is actively used to secure investment in corrective action, with outcomes tracked.
score_5_desc: Cost-impact reporting is systematic, real-time, and demonstrably drives stakeholder investment decisions.
